findings.title: Detach legacy writes from request cancellation
findings.body: The background write derives its timeout context from the original request context. HTTP request contexts are canceled when the handler returns, so returning the unified-storage result can cancel the legacy write before it starts or completes; the ten-second timeout does not prevent parent cancellation. This affects Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection and can leave legacy storage permanently out of sync after successful requests. Preserve the context values but detach request cancellation before applying the background timeout.

findings.title: Mirror the committed update rather than re-evaluating objInfo
findings.body: Legacy.Update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the updateWrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a PATCH or server-side apply operation whose result depends on the old object. Re-evaluating it against a divergent legacy object can preserve stale fields or produce a different result, even though the authoritative update succeeded. Pass a snapshot of the committed result through the wrapper so the legacy write mirrors that result rather than independently executing the update transformation.

findings.title: Preserve per-object ordering of asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: Each successful mutation launches an independent goroutine with no ordering between writes to the same object. A client can wait for Create to succeed and then issue Delete, yet the legacy Delete can execute before the legacy Create, leaving a legacy-only object after both operations finish. Likewise, two updates can reach legacy storage in reverse order and leave stale data. Serialize or sequence the background mutations per resource identity so legacy storage converges to the authoritative state.

findings.title: Do not use object names as the metric kind label
findings.body: The successful Delete path passes name to recordStorageDuration where every other path passes options.Kind. This creates a separate metric label value for every deleted object instead of grouping by kind, causing unbounded Prometheus series growth for workloads with many distinct resource names and making successful and failed deletes appear under different kinds. Pass options.Kind here.

findings.title: Attribute duration and failure metrics to the correct backend
findings.body: The background Legacy.DeleteCollection call records its result with recordStorageDuration, so each successful collection deletion records two unified-storage observations and no legacy observation; a legacy failure is incorrectly reported as a unified-storage failure. The Create and Update unified-storage error paths have the inverse mistake at lines 45 and 129, recording storage failures as legacy failures. Correct these recorder selections so backend latency and error metrics accurately identify the failing store.
